messages:
alex: Hey team — staging terraform plan is hanging during the remote refresh after the provider bump (we upgraded aws provider + moved an alias). Not sure if it's a lock or an import mismatch. Anyone around to eyeball?
priya: I can take a look in ~15m. Which module is it hanging on?
alex: It's the k8s SA & iam binding module. Plan output just stops after `Refreshing state...` for a long time. No obvious error, just no progress.
sam: Did you try `TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform refresh`? sometimes provider chain swaps trigger long list calls.
alex: Yep tried that, logs show repeated 403s for a managed role lookup, then backoff loops. Probably a creds scoping issue from the provider alias change.
josh: @alex can you paste the `provider` blocks that were changed? might be an alias or assume_role misconfig.
alex: Sure — snippet: ```hcl
provider "aws" { region = "us-west-2" }
provider "aws" { alias = "assume_ops" assume_role { role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::111111:role/ops" } }
module "k8s-sa" { source = "./modules/k8s-sa" providers = { aws = aws.assume_ops } }
```
priya: Hmm if the state still has resources created with the old provider address, terraform may try to call the wrong credentials. You can check `terraform state show module.k8s-sa.aws_iam_role.role` to see the provider id.
sam: Also check `terraform providers` to see provider addresses in the workspace. If provider addresses changed you might need `terraform state replace-provider` or `terraform import` for specific resources.
alex: I ran `terraform providers` — the module resources still reference `provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]` without alias which is surprising. We expected them to use `aws.assume_ops`.
josh: That suggests the import/creation was done before the provider map in the module was updated. Replacing provider addresses in state is usually safer than force-unlock. Example: `terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws:assume_ops'` (double-check syntax).
priya: Yes, and before doing that, create a state backup and run `terraform state list` and `terraform state show` for a couple of target resources to confirm.
alex: We don't want to do anything destructive in staging late at night. Is there a safe quick unblock to get the plan to finish so we can validate other changes?
sam: If refresh is stuck because a call keeps 403ing, a quick workaround is to set a short `max_retries` or temporarily give read-only permissions to the role so lookups succeed, then revert. But that requires IAM change.
josh: Another fast option: run `terraform plan -refresh=false -target=module.k8s-sa` to skip refresh for that module and see the rest of the plan. Won't be ideal but helps unblock other work.
alex: Good call — trying `-refresh=false -target=module.k8s-sa` now.
terra-bot: Deploybot: New commit pushed to branch `provider-bump-staging` — CI started. (CI links: https://ci.internal/build/2345) :gear:
priya: If you go the `state replace-provider` route, I'll pair and review the steps. We should also run a `terraform plan` with `-out` after replace and inspect diffs carefully.
alex: `-refresh=false -target` returned quick plan for other modules, thanks. For k8s-sa it still errors when targeted: `Error: AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform iam:GetRole`
sam: Ok so it's definitely creds. If you don't want to change IAM, we can import the resource using the AWS account creds that created it (if different) — `terraform import module.k8s-sa.aws_iam_role.role ROLE_NAME` then re-run plan.
josh: Alex, where is the role currently managed? maybe it was created manually or by another stack. If so, importing is the right fix.
alex: Looks like it was created by a bootstrap script in account 111111. I can reach out to infra-ops to get a short-lived token for import.
priya: If infra-ops can't help quickly, we can do state replace-provider as a temporary mapping to the new provider alias (only for staging), then mark it in the rollout notes so prod doesn't get touched.
sam: Agree but doc the change and backup state. Also run `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` so CI can catch unexpected diffs.
alex: OK I'm going to ping infra-ops and then either import (preferred) or do a replace-provider with backups. I'll post the exact commands before executing. Thanks for the quick help.
josh: Ping @infra-ops in #vendors if you don't hear back in 10m.
alex: Will do. Leaving this thread open; I'll update when I have the creds or have executed replace. :hand:
priya: Thanks — happy to pair if you want live screenshare.
terra-bot: Reminder: Please attach state snapshot to the ticket when you file a postmortem. (policy reminder)
